clue.text: Dipper bird got lions in a state

parts.note: a duck is a common water bird

indicators.note: to be in a state is to be agitated or disordered, so the letters of the two words beside it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumble
taken as written, part of the jumble

explanation.surface: A dipper, the small river bird, has caught some lions in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipper bird' reads as one name for a river bird, but 'Dipper' alone is the definition and 'bird' gives DUCK. 'in a state' scrambles GOT and LIONS into INGSTOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The old punishment chair plunged its occupant into a pond, so it was a device for dunking people: a dipper.

clue.text: Does he have his back to the wall in Guy's, for example?

definitions.text: Does he have his back to the wall in Guy's, for example?

parts.words: Does he have his back to the wall in Guy's, for example?
parts.note: two readings: a kitchen sideboard stands with its back against a wall, and at Guy's, a London teaching hospital, a surgeon's assistant who applies bandages to wounds has that title

explanation.surface: Someone at a London hospital seems to be cornered, fighting with his back to the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's is Guy's Hospital in London; a hospital dresser is the junior who dresses wounds. 'Back to the wall' suggests desperation but describes where the furniture stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a piece of kitchen furniture set against a wall, and a hospital assistant who bandages wounds.

clue.text: Price bird put up for clothing

parts.note: price means cost

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means writing it from bottom to top, so it is read backwards

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper puts a price on a stuffed bird alongside the clothes on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses EMU to UME, read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit or set of garments worn together, especially for a role or occasion, is clothing.

clue.text: Uncultivated eglantine coming out?

indicators.note: the wild rose is coming out of its shape, its letters breaking loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild rose, uncultivated, is coming into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose, so 'uncultivated' and 'coming out' (blooming) seem to describe it; 'coming out' rearranges its nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking refinement or grace, a person may be called uncultured or unpolished.

clue.text: One who knocks rock with ruler

parts.note: the Rock is the nickname of Gibraltar, often shortened to Gib
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone is knocking on a rock with a ruler, perhaps a geologist at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks' here means criticises or mocks, not taps. Gibraltar is known as the Rock, and ER (Elizabetha Regina) is the standard crossword ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone is to sneer at them, and a person who sneers or taunts is a mocker.

clue.text: Writer with no end of baggage

indicators.note: the writer's surname is given with no end, so its last letter is removed

parts.note: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: A writer arrives with an endless supply of luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baggage' is not luggage but an old disparaging word for a woman of loose morals. 'with no end' cuts the final E from TROLLOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggage is a dated insult for a shameless or disreputable woman, the same sense as slattern or hussy.

clue.text: Paint fit for a gusher?

parts.note: oil is a kind of paint used by artists
fit means healthy, in good shape

explanation.surface: Is this paint suitable for someone who gushes?
explanation.walkthrough: A gusher is a borehole spouting crude; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilled shaft that spurts crude petroleum from the ground is called a gusher.

clue.text: Established with extended reputation

parts.note: extended means lengthy, long
one's standing is one's status or reputation

explanation.surface: An established figure with a far-reaching good name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has existed for a long time is well established or of old date.

clue.text: Officially supervise lines in Old English

indicators.note: the lines are placed in the abbreviation, inside its two letters

parts.note: lines of poetry are verse

explanation.surface: Someone officially checks the lines of an Old English poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To superintend or watch over work formally is to supervise it.

clue.text: Punt left, for example, can be illicitly sold

parts.note: in football a punt is a kick, a boot
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A punt left by the river might be sold on illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' looks like a flat boat but is a kick: BOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods smuggled or made and traded without permission, such as pirated recordings or contraband liquor, are called that.

clue.text: Charge must be reduced for a spare room!

indicators.note: reduced in the sense of broken down into pieces, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A host must lower the rent for a spare room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' looks like a price cut but signals the anagram of all of CHARGE MUST BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom kept for visitors to stay in is a spare room.

clue.text: Signal from Wren's beau, taking in ancient city

indicators.note: the name takes the city in, holding it inside its letters

parts.note: Beau Geste is the novel by P. C. Wren, so his Beau is Geste
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A signal from a Christopher Wren admirer who has an old city in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: P. C. Wren wrote the Foreign Legion novel Beau Geste, so 'Wren's beau' is GESTE, not a boyfriend of the architect Christopher Wren.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement of the hands or head that conveys meaning is a signal.

clue.text: Relax and lounge in ever-changing surroundings

indicators.note: the rearranged word forms surroundings for the other piece, enclosing it
the word ever is changing, its letters swapped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to lounge is to lie about

explanation.surface: Unwind by lounging in a setting that never stops changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ever-changing' splits: EVER is changed to REVE, which surrounds LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease or alleviate tension or pain is to make it slacken, to relax it.

clue.text: Some writers expected to be brief?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some authors are expected to keep it short.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans writERS Expected; 'Some' signals that only part of the words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concise or curt in speech or writing is the same as being short and to the point.

clue.text: George is also a car driver?

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a pilot is one who drives or steers a vessel or aircraft

explanation.surface: George is a man who also drives a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' was RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot, which is why the definition is a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen's slang named the automatic flight-control system George, after a supposed extra crew member.

clue.text: Cutting turkey, say, on a plate with delight

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle registration code for Turkey, shown on car number plates
to delight is to charm, to enchant

explanation.surface: A diner is carving a turkey on a plate with great delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' is not the bird but the country, and its plate is a car number plate: TR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is sharp, incisive and penetrating.

clue.text: Modern way to protect king in city

parts.note: modern means new
in chess, castling is a move that tucks the king safely behind a rook

explanation.surface: A modern scheme to keep the king safe somewhere in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a large city in north-east England.

clue.text: Western locust, for example, is an enormous thing

parts.note: locusts and grasshoppers are known as hoppers

explanation.surface: A western locust is a huge creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusually large, or a huge lie, is called a monster or a whacker.

clue.text: Heather supports a month the country

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece supports another by sitting beneath it

parts.note: Erica is the botanical name of heather

explanation.surface: Heather supports a month of the year in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by the continent's name.

clue.text: Grab a bit of air?

explanation.walkthrough: An air is a tune, and a catch is a short round sung by several voices, so 'a bit of air' is musical, not a breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize or take hold of something; also a brief part-song or round in music, a little tune.

clue.text: Bury formerly in a state?

indicators.note: the word for formerly is placed in the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation of California, a US state
formerly means once, at an earlier time

explanation.surface: Was someone once buried in an American state?
explanation.definitionFit: To bury something is to hide it from view.

clue.text: Can one get up in attempt to make a threesome?

indicators.note: the turned pieces go in the attempt, inside its letters

parts.note: an attempt is a try

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means going upwards, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Can a single person rise in an effort to form a trio?
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' turns TIN and I to INIT, which sits in TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian doctrine of three persons in one God, or any group of three, is a triad.

clue.text: Evening out expected of these people?

definitions.text: Evening out expected of these people?

parts.words: Evening out expected of these people?
parts.note: 'evening out' read not as a night on the town but as making creases flat, the household job of those who press clothes

explanation.surface: Which people would be expected to go out for the evening?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' is not the time of day but the act of making even, smoothing the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: People who press laundry with a hot appliance make cloth smooth and level.

clue.text: Girl featured in new issue

indicators.note: the word issue in a new form, with its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A girl appears in the latest edition of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new issue' reads as a fresh edition, but 'new' rearranges ISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name.

clue.text: Study hard in Settle, say

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
firm means hard, solid

explanation.surface: Someone is studying hard in the Yorkshire town of Settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a town in North Yorkshire, but here it is the verb: to settle an arrangement is to make it definite.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a booking or arrangement is to make it definite, to ratify it.

clue.text: Greenpeace leader endlessly affected about English fish in aquaria…

indicators.note: the leader of the group's name is its first letter
the trimmed word goes about the abbreviation, around it
the word for affected loses its end, its last letter dropped

parts.note: uppish means snooty or affected

explanation.surface: The head of Greenpeace is endlessly affected by the plight of English fish kept in tanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts UPPISH to UPPIS, which goes 'about' E to give UPPIES after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Small brightly coloured tropical freshwater species are favourites in home tanks.

clue.text: 5 and bitter if we cooked this fish

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: '5 and bitter if we cooked this fish (7)'. ALE (bitter) + anagram of IF WE gives the fish, but the leading '5 and' has no job: it does not define or build the answer, and no search found the clue's original text.
annotationWithheld.clue: 5 and bitter if we cooked this fish

clue.text: A mannerly lot turning out in showy style

indicators.note: the phrase turning out suggests the group being turned inside out, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A polite crowd turns out dressed up in flamboyant fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' reads as arriving or dressing up but rearranges all twelve letters of A MANNERLY LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: In a decorative, flashy manner, done for show rather than use.
